text:
Gabe Perreault is 21, in his first real NHL season, and he's scoring like a top-six winger: 7 goals and 11 points in 22 games for the Rangers on about 16 and a half minutes a night. Flashscore credited him with leading the Rangers to a big win in Vancouver on Nov. 14, when he had a goal and an assist.

The scoring looks mostly earned. His 6.1 expected goals is a strong number for his ice time, and he's only about a goal ahead of it. The Rangers get about 53% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on at five on five, though they're out-attempted in those minutes, which says the shots he's around are good ones. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking (a small sample) had 60% of his shots coming off the rush.

Some context from the draft: forwards picked 18th to 28th since 2005 averaged a median 0.37 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.50. Wyatt Johnston, also a 23rd pick, posted the same 0.50 as a rookie. What to watch is whether New York keeps him in a scoring role through the winter.
